title: Right-to-erasure test on vector store
objective: Submit a query containing a fabricated personal identifier, confirm (via retrieval) it is embedded/stored, then test whether there is any mechanism to delete it from ChromaDB.
input_scenario: Submit/retrieve a marker string, then check agent3 module for any delete/erasure API.
expected_behavior: A data-subject erasure mechanism exists, or submitted free-text queries are not persisted into the vector store at all.

actual_behavior.sent: check whether queries get added to the 'incidents' collection, and whether any delete API exists

severity_justification_hint: Absence of an erasure mechanism is a compliance gap (e.g. GDPR Art. 17) if personal data ever enters the store.
observations: The retrieval returned an existing incident record, but the evidence does not confirm whether user queries are stored in ChromaDB or whether a deletion/erasure mechanism exists.
conclusion: The right-to-erasure capability could not be conclusively evaluated from the provided evidence.
